findings.claim: Any callback whose state has enroll: true deletes every TOTP factor except the newest one, without checking that a new factor was actually enrolled during the round-trip or recording which factors existed beforehand. A user with multiple TOTP devices who starts enrollment but reaches the callback without a new factor being added (e.g. the enrollment Action is skipped or misconfigured) will have an existing, still-used device deleted with no recovery.

The created_at field used to sort factors is validated only as z.string(), so Date.parse can return NaN for malformed values, making the sort order arbitrary and risking that the wrong (still-in-use) device is identified as newest and kept while a valid one is deleted.

Any error during factor cleanup is caught and only logged as a warning, after which login proceeds normally and neither the user nor the frontend is told that the old factor was not removed, so a lost or compromised device can remain enrolled while the user believes it was cleaned up.

There are no tests covering the new controller behavior: that cleanup only runs for enrollment states, that a cleanup failure does not block login, that the enroll parameter rejects values other than true, and that GET oidc/mfa/authenticators returns 403 without a session; reverting the controller's enrollment branch today would not fail any test.
There is no test verifying that ext-enroll-otp is added to the authorization URL.

The cached Management API token is never cleared after receiving a 401 or 403 response, so a token issued before required scopes were granted keeps failing for up to its full lifetime (Auth0's default is 24 hours) instead of being refreshed.

A tenant-wide Management API token capable of listing and deleting any user's MFA factors is stored in Redis unencrypted under a single global key, which is riskier than the existing pattern used for Firebase tokens because of the greater damage this token can cause if exposed.

Three new entity schemas (MfaEnrollmentSession, otp-code.entity.ts, and auth0-otp-association.entity.ts) are added but nothing in the codebase currently uses them; they should either be wired up (e.g. using MfaEnrollmentSession.supersededIds for the cleanup fix) or removed.

The documentation is not updated to describe the new enroll parameter, the new endpoint, or the new deployment requirement that the Auth0 application needs a Management API grant with read: and delete:authentication_methods scopes; that requirement currently exists only as a code comment.
@ApiOkResponse has no response type specified because Authenticator is a TypeScript type rather than a DTO class, so Swagger cannot document the response shape.
created_at values are cast with 'as string', an unsafe cast that a type guard or the created_at schema change would eliminate.
